papers.title: Influenza activity in the United States during the 2025-26 influenza season
papers.abstract: Background Comprehensive influenza surveillance is conducted year-round in the United States to monitor changes in influenza activity. This report summarizes the 2025-26 U.S. influenza season. Methods Data from September 28, 2025 through October 3, 2026 were collected from national surveillance systems monitoring influenza through laboratory testing, outpatient and emergency department visits, hospitalizations, and mortality. Data modeled disease burden and assessed severity using established criteria. A subset of influenza positive specimens were genetically and antigenically characterized and assessed for antiviral susceptibility. Results Influenza activity peaked during the week ending December 27, 2025, five weeks earlier than the 2024-25 season. There were two waves of influenza activity with influenza A(H3N2) subclade K viruses predominating the season overall and during the first wave followed by a smaller B/Victoria wave. The majority of circulating A(H3N2) and B/Victoria viruses were antigenically drifted from 2025-26 influenza vaccine reference strains. Season severity was classified as moderate overall, with children (0-17 years old) experiencing a high severity season and adults experiencing a moderate severity season. Children experienced the highest percent of influenza-associated outpatient and emergency department visits compared to other age groups. This season's cumulative influenza-associated hospitalization rate in children is the highest hospitalization rate in the past 16 years. Additionally, there were 198 influenza-associated pediatric deaths reported to CDC as of October 29, 2026. Conclusions Although antigenically drifted A(H3N2) viruses predominated, the 2025-26 U.S. influenza season occurred within historic norms for timing and severity. Year-round surveillance remains critical for detecting changes in influenza viruses and monitoring influenza-associated morbidity and mortality.

papers.title: Colorectal cancer incidence and mortality trends by age at onset in South Africa from 2002 to 2023
papers.abstract: Background: Colorectal cancer is the third most common cancer in men and women, and the fifth most common cancer overall, in South Africa. A previous report by the South African National Cancer Registry (SANCR) established that colorectal cancer incidence is rising in all South African population groups but rising fastest in Black South Africans. However, whether incidence increases by age at onset, as observed in many upper-income countries worldwide, remains unknown. In the present study, we assessed changes in colorectal cancer incidence (2002-2023) and mortality (2002-2019) in South Africa by sex, population group and age at onset. Methods: We calculated incidence from SANCR case counts and mortality from Stats SA death records, using Stats SA mid-year population estimates, standardised to the Segi world standard population. We defined age at onset as early (less than 50 years) or late (50 years or older). We described trends using joinpoint regression and annual percentage changes (APCs) over 2002-2023 and 2011-2023, the period after private-laboratory reporting became mandatory. Results: A total of 70,467 histologically confirmed primary colorectal cancers were registered with the SANCR over 2002-2023; 53.7% were in men. The overall age-standardised incidence rate (ASIR) was 6.61 per 100,000 (95% CI 6.32-6.89) in 2002 and 8.23 (7.99-8.46) in 2023. Overall incidence fell from 2002 to 2007 (not significant), rose from 2007 to 2015 and showed no significant change from 2015 to 2023. The first two segments coincide with the withdrawal of some private laboratories from reporting in 2005-2007 and with mandatory reporting from 2011. From 2011 to 2023, incidence fell in White South Africans (APC -1.0%, 95% CI -1.9 to -0.04), rose in Black African South Africans (+3.1%, 2.0 to 4.2) and did not change significantly in Coloured (-1.0%, -2.3 to 0.3) or Indian/Asian (+0.3%, -2.2 to 2.7) South Africans. Early-onset incidence rose by 1.6% per year (95% CI 1.1 to 2.1) over 2002-2023, similar to late-onset incidence (1.8%, 1.0 to 2.5). After 2011, neither changed significantly (early-onset +0.3%, -0.3 to 0.9; late-onset 0.0%, -1.0 to 1.0). Over 2002-2023, the early-onset APC was highest in White South Africans (+3.9%, 2.9 to 4.9), followed by Black African (+1.7%, 1.1 to 2.4), Coloured (+1.6%, 1.0 to 2.3) and Indian/Asian (+1.5%, 0.4 to 2.7) South Africans. The late-onset APC was +4.1% (3.4 to 4.9) in Black African, +1.3% (0.1 to 2.5) in White, +1.3% (0.1 to 2.5) in Indian/Asian and +0.7% (-0.3 to 1.6) in Coloured South Africans. After 2011, early-onset incidence rose in White (+1.2%, 0.3 to 2.2), Coloured (+1.7%, 0.4 to 3.1) and Black African (+1.1%, 0.4 to 1.8) South Africans. Late-onset incidence fell in White South Africans (-1.5%, -2.6 to -0.4) and rose in Black African South Africans (+3.7%, 2.4 to 5.0). Early-onset mortality rose by 1.2% per year (0.5 to 2.0) over 2002-2019, and late-onset mortality by 0.9% (0.3 to 1.4). Conclusion: Early-onset colorectal cancer incidence in South Africa rose over 2002-2023, and much of the rise coincided with mandatory private-laboratory reporting from 2011. Since 2011, early-onset incidence has risen modestly in White, Coloured and Black African South Africans, while late-onset incidence has fallen in White South Africans. In Black African South Africans, late-onset incidence and mortality continue to rise faster than early-onset.

papers.title: The plateau in liver disease mortality in Germany: contrasting trends by age, region and ICD-10 code, 2000-2024
papers.abstract: Background: Cirrhosis is often diagnosed only at decompensation, making identification of high-risk groups important for prevention and early detection. Chronic liver disease mortality has fallen in southern Europe and France since 2010, but not in Germany. Whether the German plateau reflects birth-cohort alcohol exposure, metabolic liver disease or certification practice is unknown. Methods: Deaths by ICD-10 code, sex and age group were extracted from the WHO Mortality Database for 16 European countries (2000-2022), with Eurostat rates (2011-2023), German state-level mortality (1998-2024) and hospital diagnoses (2000-2023). Registry and Global Burden of Disease Study (GBD) 2023 estimates were summarised for ages 45-64, 65-74 and 75 years and over, with registry rates standardised to the European Standard Population 2013. Findings: Germany's age-standardised chronic liver disease mortality was 16.6 per 100 000 in 2011 and 16.0 in 2023, against declines of 21-37% in France, Italy and Spain. Between 2010 and 2022, alcoholic liver disease mortality at ages 45-64 fell by 17% in men and 25% in women, whereas fibrosis and cirrhosis (K74) mortality at ages 65-74 rose by 27% and 28%, with larger K70-K77 mortality increases in eastern than western Germany. Hospitalisation rates showed similar age-specific patterns, while in-hospital case fatality declined. Fewer than 0.5% of liver deaths were certified as fatty liver. GBD 2023 showed a similar age-specific increase but attributed rising mortality to all five modelled aetiologies. Interpretation: The German plateau reflects continued decline below age 65 and rising mortality at ages 65-74, compatible with cohorts born 1945-59 reaching this age band, particularly in eastern Germany. Consumption records and surveys indicate differing regional patterns of alcohol exposure. Much of the cirrhosis in these cohorts is certified without aetiology, and GBD's aetiological estimates cannot be verified in registration data. Funding: None.

papers.title: Delivered but Discharged Without Assessment: A National Multilevel Analysis of Missed Maternal Postpartum Assessment Before Discharge After Facility Birth in Ethiopia, 2024/2025 EDHS
papers.abstract: Abstract Background: Missed maternal postnatal assessment before discharge after facility birth is an undermeasured indicator of intrafacility quality of care that previous Ethiopian studies did not isolate in nationally representative analyses. This gap matters because women may reach facilities for childbirth yet leave without a basic maternal clinical assessment during the highest-risk postpartum period, making missed assessment a marker of effective coverage failure rather than conventional postnatal care utilization alone. Methods: We analyzed nationally representative 2024-2025 Ethiopia Demographic and Health Survey data for 3,645 women aged 15-49 years whose most recent live birth occurred in a health facility. All analyses incorporated sampling weights and survey design features. Factors associated with missed maternal postnatal assessment before discharge were examined using multilevel mixed-effects logistic regression accounting for clustering within enumeration areas, with adjusted odds ratios (AORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) reported. Results: Overall, 40.1% (95% CI: 37.0-43.3) of women who delivered in Ethiopian health facilities did not receive a maternal postnatal assessment before discharge. Missed assessment was less likely after caesarean birth than vaginal delivery (AOR 0.32, 95% CI 0.19-0.53) and among women with at least one pregnancy complication (AOR 0.46, 95% CI 0.34-0.63). Antenatal care showed a dose-response association, with lower odds among women with 4-7 visits (AOR 0.49, 95% CI 0.27-0.89) and [≥]8 visits (AOR 0.43, 95% CI 0.23-0.81) than among women with no antenatal care. Geographic inequities persisted after adjustment, including higher odds in Somali (AOR 2.07, 95% CI 1.02-4.18). Conclusions: A substantial proportion of facility births in Ethiopia end without a maternal assessment before discharge, indicating that institutional delivery coverage can overestimate effective postpartum care when discharge processes are weak. Improving maternal outcomes will require universal pre-discharge assessment standards, stronger discharge documentation, and targeted quality-improvement efforts in underserved regions. For international maternal health policy, facility birth should not be counted as effective coverage unless every woman is assessed before she goes home.

papers.title: Cross-informant validation of the Pica, ARFID, and Rumination Disorder Interview in adolescents: Agreement between child and parent reports
papers.abstract: Background: Reliable assessment of avoidant/restrictive food intake disorder (ARFID) in young people may require information from both children and caregivers, yet cross-informant agreement has not been examined for the Pica, ARFID, and Rumination Disorder Interview (PARDI). This study evaluated agreement between child and parent PARDI interviews for ARFID diagnosis, individual DSM-5 Criterion A, ARFID dimensions, and overall severity. Methods: Twenty children aged 11-14 years screening positive for ARFID and one parent per child were recruited from the ARFID InitiativE Sweden (ARIES) cohort. Children and parents completed separate PARDI interviews with trained interviewers. Parent-child agreement was assessed using percentage agreement and Cohens kappa ({kappa}) for categorical ratings of ARFID diagnosis and Criterion A consequences. For continuous ratings of ARFID dimensions and overall severity, agreement was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs) and paired t-tests comparing mean parent and child scores. Results: Parents gave higher mean scores than children across all continuous domains, although the difference was statistically significant only for overall severity (raw mean difference=0.42, p=.003). Parent-child agreement was poor for sensory sensitivity (ICC=0.42), moderate for lack of interest (ICC=0.63) and overall severity (ICC=0.71), and excellent for concern about aversive consequences (ICC=0.95). ARFID was identified in 17/20 parent interviews and 14/20 child interviews; diagnostic agreement was 75% ({kappa}=0.31, p=.133). Agreement was perfect (100%) for Criterion A1, high for A2 and A3 (both 95%), and lowest for psychosocial impairment (A4; 65% agreement, {kappa}=0.19). Item-level findings indicated a general tendency toward higher parental ratings, although children provided higher ratings on selected items involving food restriction, sensory experiences, hunger cues, and abdominal pain. Conclusions: Child and parent PARDI interviews provided overlapping but non-interchangeable information. Agreement varied across different aspects of ARFID, with greater discrepancies for psychosocial impairment and sensory sensitivity. These differences may partly reflect what children and parents are able to observe or experience directly. Multi-informant assessment may therefore offer a more complete account of pediatric ARFID than either response alone.

papers.title: Widening racial and ethnic disparities in Helicobacter pylori infection in the United States: a Bayesian meta-analytic catalytic model of age-specific forces of infection
papers.abstract: Background Helicobacter pylori is the main cause of non-cardia gastric cancer. In the U.S. H. pylori seroprevalence has declined. However, whether all subgroups have benefited equally from this change is unclear. Further, prevalence alone cannot indicate when infection risk is most acute and thus when to target prevention efforts like screening. Methods We synthesized age-stratified H. pylori seroprevalence data from 36 U.S. studies (N=56,845; 1965-2014), identified via literature search through September 2022. We fitted Bayesian hierarchical catalytic epidemic models to estimate, by race/ethnicity (for each of five race/ethnicity groups) and birth cohort (pre-1960 vs. 1960+, or continuous), the maximum proportion infected, age-specific force of infection (FOI), and the age at half-maximum seroprevalence. Findings Disparities in maximum prevalence worsened in the 1960+ birth cohort, with the absolute Hispanic-Non-Hispanic White (NHW) gap widening from 33.2 to 51.4 percentage points. FOIs peaked at the youngest ages for the Non-Hispanic American Indian/Alaska Native (AI/AN) and Non-Hispanic Black (NHB) populations. Age patterns varied independently of burden; Hispanic and AI/AN populations reached similar peak prevalence (83.0% vs 76.1%) for the 1960+ birth cohort, yet the age at half-maximum seroprevalence was 19.3 years (95%CrI: 14.9, 23.5) vs 3.20 years (95%CrI: 1.99, 4.63). Continuous birth-cohort analyses supported these findings. Interpretation National declines in H. pylori mask widening racial and ethnic disparities. In AI/AN and NHB populations, seroprevalence rises steeply in early childhood, well before adulthood-targeted screen-and-treat programs would intervene. Moreover, similar peak prevalence can mask different age patterns of infection, and should be accounted for when guiding prevention strategies. Funding National Cancer Institute U01CA265729 and U01CA319219

papers.title: SARS-CoV-2 antibody landscape following multiple vaccinations and infections during Omicron period
papers.abstract: Background: Repeated COVID-19 vaccination effects on the immunogenicity, breadth, and durability of antibody responses across antigenically distinct SARS-CoV-2 variants remain incompletely understood. Method: Participants receiving >= five COVID-19 vaccine doses 2020-2025 were selected from a prospective cohort in Michigan. Serum IgG, IgM, and ACE2 percent inhibition were measured using multiplex assays. Baseline-adjusted immunogenicity, cross-reactivity, and formulation-specific antibody durability were evaluated using regression models. Result: Twenty-one participants were included (median: seven vaccine doses). For every two-fold increase in pre-vaccination IgG concentration, post-vaccination fold-rise was 34% (95% CI: 16%-48%), 43% (95% CI: 15%-62%), and 55% (95% CI: 21%-75%) lower following monovalent, bivalent, and 2023-24 vaccination, while baseline-adjusted immunogenicity showed no significant trends across successive vaccines. Antibody landscapes demonstrated broad cross-reactivity against ancestral and Omicron variants, with similar strain-specific IgG changes across ancestral, vaccine-matched, and antigenically distant strains, but greater heterogeneity in ACE2 inhibition. Formulation-specific waning models showed significant IgG declines following monovalent and bivalent vaccination (beta = -1.03, 95% CI: -1.51 to -0.55; P<0.001 and -1.00 , 95% CI: -1.71 to -0.30; P=0.007, respectively) and ACE2 inhibition declines following monovalent vaccination, while other formulations showed less consistent changes. Despite waning, antibody levels generally remained relatively high across variants up to 300 days post-vaccination, with formulation-specific differences in durability. Conclusion: Repeated COVID-19 vaccination maintained baseline-adjusted immunogenicity and broad cross-reactive antibody responses, with formulation-specific differences in durability. Higher baseline immunity was associated with smaller post-vaccination increases, suggesting repeated boosting continues to reinforce humoral immunity despite increasingly complex immune histories.

papers.title: Multidrug-Resistant Tuberculosis Rates Among High-Risk Populations in Brazil: An Analysis from 2001 to 2021
authors: C. Dailton Guedes de Oliveira Moraes
papers.abstract: Multidrug-Resistant Tuberculosis (MDR-TB) represents a global public health threat, with a rising prevalence, particularly among vulnerable populations. This cross-sectional study analyzed MDR-TB notifications in Brazil from 2001 to 2021, using data from DATASUS, and stratified by periods and risk groups (HIV-positive individuals, smokers, drug users, healthcare workers, incarcerated individuals, and people experiencing homelessness). Descriptive analyses and parametric statistical tests (ANOVA and Tukey, p less than 0.05) were applied. A significant increase in cases was observed across all groups, especially between 2017 and 2021, with growth ranging from 294% to 574% depending on the population. Factors such as treatment abandonment, coinfection, social vulnerability, and occupational exposure were key determinants for MDR-TB dissemination. The findings indicate that current public health policies are insufficient, highlighting the urgent need for targeted prevention strategies, therapeutic follow-up, and control measures for high-risk populations.

papers.title: Multi-omics models for hypertension prediction using blood pressure PRS and omics scores
papers.abstract: Background: Hypertension is a major modifiable risk factor for cardiovascular disease, yet the relative contributions of proteomic (ProtS), metabolomic (MetS), and polygenic risk scores (PRS) to incident hypertension risk remain incompletely characterized. Methods: We developed ProtS and MetS for systolic (SBP) and diastolic blood pressure (DBP), and hypertension using Elastic Net regression in the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (MESA). We incorporated these scores with previously developed BP PRSs into 5 incremental XGBoost models, with external validation in the Jackson Heart Study (JHS). We further applied transfer learning to adapt the MESA-derived models to JHS. Elastic Net selected proteins were prioritized using Mendelian randomization, colocalization, and functional analyses. Results: In MESA, model discrimination improved with the addition of omics scores, with the combined model achieving an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.72 compared with 0.63 for the clinical baseline model. In JHS, ProtS showed the highest AUC of 0.68 and the smallest cross-cohort performance decline, compared to MetS and PRS. Incorporating measured SBP and DBP substantially improved discrimination, with the PRS+BP model achieving an AUC of 0.80 in MESA and the baseline+BP model achieving an AUC of 0.74 in JHS. Among JHS participants with normal baseline BP, ProtS provided the strongest discrimination among models without measured BP (AUC = 0.62), while PRS+BP model achieved an AUC of 0.69. Leaf-weight refreshing consistently improved calibration in JHS while preserving discrimination. Mendelian randomization identified 77 proteins associated with BP traits or hypertension, involved in vascular, inflammatory, renal, and natriuretic pathways. Conclusions: ProtS demonstrated superior predictive performance and cross-cohort transferability among the omics modalities evaluated, while measured BP remained the strongest predictors of incident hypertension. Proteomic and genetic information may provide complementary biological signals for identifying individuals at elevated hypertension risk, particularly before clinically elevated BP is detectable.

papers.title: Beyond National Averages: Social Contact Patterns in the Upper Midwest
papers.abstract: Background: Social contact surveys measure how individuals interact with each other, which directly influences disease transmission dynamics. The COVID-19 pandemic substantially altered how people live and work, highlighting the need for up-to-date and sub-national estimates of social contact patterns to inform disease modeling and public health planning. Methods: The Midwest Analytics & Disease Modeling Center (MADMC) conducted an opt-in social contact survey of upper Midwest residents, with about 60% of participants drawn from Minnesota. Participants reported all interpersonal contacts during the previous day, including the age of their contacts allowing for the analysis of mixing patterns. Detailed demographic information about the participants was also collected, allowing for additional subgroup analyses of contact patterns. Results: Participants in our sample had an average of 6.8 contacts per day (IQR: 2.0 - 8.0), which is within the range of recent post-pandemic US national and European estimates. Contacts varied across demographic groups, with those attending work or school in-person reporting the highest number of contacts. Mixing across most age group pairs was a little lower than in comparable national survey except for younger age groups, who had substantially higher rates of contact with same-age peers. Differences in the contact matrices alone were associated with a 6.7% difference in estimated basic reproduction number(R0). Near the epidemic threshold, even this modest difference could meaningfully affect transmission dynamics. These effects may be amplified or attenuated by pathogen-specific age patterns of susceptibility and infectiousness, leading to larger or smaller differences in R0 estimates derived from national versus regional mixing patterns. Conclusions: These findings provide empirical evidence on post-pandemic social contact patterns in the United States and highlight the potential implications of regional variation in social mixing for infectious disease transmission. The mean 6.8 daily contacts is consistent with evidence of persistent changes in daily routines following the pandemic. Incorporating contemporary, region-specific contact patterns into transmission models may improve their ability to capture geographic variation in transmission risk and inform epidemic forecasting.

papers.title: Wastewater sequence data reveal national and cross-border virus transmission dynamics
papers.abstract: Spatial epidemic models estimate disease transmission counts between populations using human mobility data, but location-to-location transmission is rarely observed directly. To address this gap, we develop mutation-counting methods to infer transmission structure from viral genetic variation measured in wastewater. In epidemic simulations with known transmission networks, our primary estimator robustly recovers spatial structure under realistic mutation-detection limits. Applied to spatiotemporal SARS-CoV-2 wastewater data from Austria, the method reveals strong seasonal reorganization, with inferred transmission becoming more geographically localized in winter and more dispersed in summer. We further identify locations with systematically higher or lower connectivity than expected from commuting, with temporal changes coinciding with regional restrictions, reopening and tourism. We then test whether such inference remains possible across national borders, recovering coherent spatial structure and temporal variation in connectivity between Austria, Switzerland and Liechtenstein. These results establish wastewater sequence data as a promising complement to mobility data for monitoring spatial transmission and detecting changes in epidemic spread associated with seasonality and interventions.

papers.title: Emergent Heterogeneity in Compartmental Disease Models
papers.abstract: Heterogeneity in infectious disease spread reshapes the risk and severity of outbreaks. This heterogeneity can arise from intrinsic individual-level differences in susceptibility, contact patterns, and infectious durations. Heterogeneity can also emerge from disease dynamics in a canonically homogeneous population, due to the fact that individuals randomly become infected at different times, recover after different intervals, and have access to different numbers of susceptible individuals. Here, we explore the mechanisms generating emergent heterogeneity by analyzing secondary case distributions within the SIR model. We show numerically and prove analytically that the variation in secondary cases, calculated over the course of the epidemic, does not change with R0. This is in contrast to the increasing variation in secondary cases in the linearized SIR model, often used to study heterogeneity at the beginning of an outbreak. When we consider "forward cohorts" of individuals infected at the same time, between-cohort variation increases as R0 increases, while within-cohort variation decreases. We show that these effects balance exactly, leading to the invariance of the variation in secondary cases with respect to R0. These results demonstrate the importance of considering emergent, as well as intrinsic, variation between individuals and of considering heterogeneity of transmission spread over the whole epidemic cycle, including substantive dynamical effects that appear even in the initial outbreak phase.

papers.title: Nirsevimab effectiveness against RSV hospitalizations in children 8-23 months at risk of severe RSV
papers.abstract: Importance: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of hospitalization in high-risk young children during their second RSV season. Nirsevimab, a long-acting monoclonal antibody against RSV, is recommended for some children who are at increased risk for severe RSV and entering their second RSV season to prevent severe RSV disease. Because of limited eligibility criteria for second season nirsevimab, estimating its effectiveness is challenging. Objective: We evaluated nirsevimab effectiveness against RSV-associated hospitalizations among young children eligible to receive nirsevimab during their second RSV season. Design: This retrospective case control study with a test-negative design was conducted during the 2024-2025 and 2025-2026 RSV seasons. Setting: Enrollment was in 26 hospitals across 24 U.S. states. Participants: Children eligible for nirsevimab during their second RSV season (as recommended in August 2023) were included. Nirsevimab-eligible children 8-23 months old hospitalized with respiratory symptoms were enrolled. Case-patients tested positive for RSV; control-patients tested negative for RSV. Exposures: Receipt of nirsevimab before or during the second RSV season and at least 7 days before symptom onset. Outcomes and measures: RSV-associated hospitalization. We estimated nirsevimab effectiveness using multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age, month and year of hospitalization, census region, and sex comparing the odds of second season nirsevimab receipt among case- and control-patients. Results: One hundred six case-patients and 125 control-patients were analyzed. Distributions of age, sex, race and ethnicity, and region were similar in case- and control-patients. Most case- and control-patients were eligible for nirsevimab because of chronic lung disease of prematurity (84.0% and 69.6%, respectively). Overall, 21 (19.8%) of case-patients and 53 (42.4%) of control-patients received nirsevimab. Adjusted nirsevimab effectiveness against RSV-associated hospitalizations was 78.1% (95% CI, 55.2%-89.3%); the median interval from nirsevimab receipt to symptom onset was 66.5 days (IQR = 30-96 days). Effectiveness was estimated to be higher if nirsevimab was received 8-59 days before symptom onset (88.5%, 95% CI, 63.4%-96.4%). Conclusions: This analysis provides real-world estimates of substantial nirsevimab effectiveness against RSV-associated hospitalizations for high-risk U.S. children in their second RSV season These data support recommendations for nirsevimab as a preventive strategy in this population.

papers.title: Population-level indirect effects of HPV vaccination in high-income settings: a Bayesian modelling study
papers.abstract: Background Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination provides direct protection to vaccinated individuals, but also indirectly protects unvaccinated individuals through reduced HPV transmission. Mechanistic transmission models that predict the magnitude of such effects have been crucial to informing vaccination strategies. However, nearly two decades of post-vaccination experience in high-income countries now allow us to empirically characterise how population-level indirect effects vary with vaccine coverage, time since vaccine introduction, and age. Methods We synthesised studies reporting HPV16/18 prevalence before and after vaccine introduction in high-income settings between 2007 and 2025. Indirect effects were estimated as the observed reduction in HPV16/18 prevalence after accounting for expected direct vaccine protection. We used a Bayesian hierarchical model to examine associations with vaccine coverage, time since vaccine introduction, and age at effect assessment across routine, catch-up, and non-targeted vaccination groups. XGBoost was used as a complementary, non-parametric approach. Findings Data from 11 high-income settings were included. Indirect effects increased during the first five to eight years after vaccine introduction and then remained relatively stable. Indirect effects generally decreased with increasing vaccine coverage. Patterns with age differed across vaccination groups. In the routine group, indirect effects increased during adolescence and remained positive at older observed ages. In the catch-up group, indirect effects decreased with age and approached zero or became negative after approximately age 25 years. XGBoost identified similar non-linear patterns. Interpretation Indirect protection against HPV16/18 develops gradually after vaccine introduction and varies with vaccine coverage, age, and vaccination group. This empirical approach can complement transmission models by using real-world evidence to characterise population-level indirect protection. However, making predictions outside the populations and ranges represented in the data should be done cautiously.

papers.title: An integrative eco-entomovirological study of Culicoides species associated with Oropouche virus in Colombia
papers.abstract: Background Oropouche virus (OROV) causes recurrent outbreaks in South America, including Colombia. Although Culicoides paraensis is the principal recognized urban vector, the potential involvement of other Culicoides species remains incompletely understood. In Colombia, studies combining viral detection, host-feeding behavior, and ecological suitability are scarce. Methodology We investigated Culicoides communities in urban and peri-urban environments of Puerto Carreno, Vichada, during two seasonal transitions. Species identification combined morphology and COI DNA barcoding, and blood-meal sources were identified using vertebrate molecular markers. OROV RNA was assessed by RT-qPCR targeting the L and S genomic segments, and maximum likelihood prevalence estimates with 95% confidence intervals were calculated accounting for unequal pool sizes, including a conservative estimate based on concordant detection of both targets. Selected positive samples underwent multiplex amplicon sequencing of fragments from all three OROV genomic segments (L, M, and S) using Oxford Nanopore Technology, followed by consensus reconstruction and phylogenetic analysis. Ecological suitability models were compared with reported OROV case distributions. Principal Findings We collected 1,639 specimens representing 11 taxa, eight supported by COI barcoding. C. insignis accounted for more than 70% of captures and was the only taxon collected in urban settings. OROV RNA was detected in C. insignis, C. pusillus, and C. ignacioi. In C. insignis, concordant detection of the L and S molecular targets yielded an estimated prevalence of 3.61 per 1,000 individuals (95% CI: 0.94-9.60). Nanopore sequencing recovered OROV-derived fragments spanning up to 656 nt across the L, M, and S genomic segments. Shorter fragments supported molecular identification, while phylogenetic analysis of a 656-nt M-segment region recovered from C. insignis and C. pusillus placed both sequences within a group containing viruses associated with the recent South American outbreak, although partial genomic coverage precluded formal lineage assignment. Blood-meal analyses identified feeding on humans, horses, and pigs in C. insignis; humans and horses in C. pusillus; and horses in C. ignacioi. Ecological models identified distinct environmental associations among species, and predicted suitability for overlapping portions of regions reporting OROV cases. Administrative-scale concordance was heterogeneous. Conclusions The integration of molecular, host-feeding, and ecological evidence highlights C. insignis, C. pusillus, and C. ignacioi as species of epidemiological interest in the context of OROV circulation in Colombia. These findings expand current knowledge of OROV-associated Culicoides diversity and provide a basis for targeted entomological surveillance and experimental studies to clarify their potential roles in virus transmission.

papers.title: Aging, Structural, and Neighborhood-Environmental Correlates of Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Risk Factor Burden Across U.S. Census Tracts
papers.abstract: Background. The American Heart Association defined Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic (CKM) syndrome in 2023. Census-tract studies often examined one condition without spatial modeling. It is unclear where combined Stage 1-2 burden concentrates and how it relates to aging, environment, and socioeconomic conditions. Methods. We built a CKM burden index for 70,336 tracts from five CDC PLACES crude prevalences (obesity, diabetes, hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, chronic kidney disease) and compared it with NHANES 2017-2020. In 69,530 contiguous-U.S. tracts, we fit Bayesian spatial (BYM2) models with demographic, socioeconomic, and environmental predictors and aging x environment interactions, plus descriptive machine learning. The primary model excluded behavioral measures sharing the outcome's BRFSS source; a second added them. Credible intervals (CrIs) are conditional on PLACES estimates. Results. Agreement with NHANES was modest. Burden clustered spatially (Moran's I = 0.657) and highest in the South. Behavioral measures had the largest machine-learning importance (52.6%), partly from shared sourcing. Each percentage-point increase in adults 65 years was associated with 0.112 units higher burden (95% CrI 0.111-0.113) outside low-income, low-access (LILA) tracts. LILA tracts had 0.10-0.14 units higher burden from the 25th aging percentile but not consistently in the youngest decile. Aging and socioeconomic associations held across sensitivity analyses. The primary model's residual Southern excess approached zero after adding behavioral measures, which may reflect shared measurement, real differences in these behaviors, or both. Conclusions. CKM burden is spatially clustered and highest in the South. LILA tracts had modestly higher burden above the youngest tracts. These cross-sectional estimates support area-level surveillance and needs assessment.

papers.title: Gut microbiome associations with incident cardiovascular disease in Nordic populations
papers.abstract: Background: The gut microbiome is an emerging risk factor for cardiovascular disease. However, there is a lack of large-scale metagenomic studies with replication that identify gut microbial features associated with incident cardiovascular disease (CVD). Methods: We tested for gut microbiome associations with CVD using metagenomes from stool samples in a discovery-replication framework across four large prospective Nordic cohorts with 635 incident CVD in 11,604 participants in the discovery cohort and 2,309 incident CVD in 20,965 participants combined across three replication cohorts. Results: Higher Shannon diversity index and species richness were consistently associated with a lower risk of incident CVD. In addition, the relative abundance of nine species and eleven bacterial functional modules showed reproducible associations with incident CVD in the discovery cohort and in a meta-analysis of the three replication cohorts. We identified a female-specific gut microbiota-related pathway involving the prevalent oral-gut species Rothia mucilaginosa_A, enriched among denture users, thus serving as a proxy for longstanding poor oral health. Mendelian randomization analysis supported a causal effect of denture use on increased relative abundance of Rothia mucilaginosa_A. This pathway was linked to increased CVD risk through altered gut microbial manganese transport, elevated circulating imidazole propionate levels, and increased levels of systemic inflammation biomarkers. The second pathway involved both ?-diversity metrics and the remaining eight species, all of which were strongly associated with multiple markers of metabolic syndrome and with bacterial pathways related to purine metabolism, microbial stress responses, altered redox balance, ascorbic acid degradation, and branched chain amino acid biosynthesis. Conclusions: These findings demonstrate that gut microbiota diversity, specific taxa, and functional pathways provide new insights into the underlying biology of CVD. Furthermore, these findings suggest that the link between poor oral health and cardiovascular disease may, at least partly, operate through altered gut microbiota.

papers.title: The gut microbiome and incident atherosclerotic cardiovascular events: Prospective analyses in three Swedish cohorts
papers.abstract: Background: Variation in the gut microbiome composition has been associated with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) in case-control designs. We aimed to investigate associations with incident ASCVD events applying a prospective design to reduce the impact of reverse causality. Methods: We assessed associations between gut microbiome features measured by shotgun metagenomic sequencing and incident total ASCVD, ischemic heart disease (IHD) and ischemic stroke, including fatal and non-fatal events as defined by registry follow-up in 17,216 participants from three Swedish population-based cohorts (SCAPIS, SIMPLER, and MOS). Results from Cox proportional hazards regression models adjusted for demographic, and lifestyle factors, medication, and prevalent diabetes were combined across cohorts using a fixed-effect meta-analysis accounting for multiple testing. Associations were tested for replication in HUNT and FINRISK. Results: During a median of 6-8 y follow-up, 769 incident ASCVD events occurred. Species diversity was inversely associated with ASCVD and IHD, with a hazard ratio for IHD of 0.86 per SD increase in species richness (95% CI: 0.79-0.95). Sixty-eight common species (i.e., present in ?30% individuals) were associated with incident IHD after adjusting for sex and birth country, but only eight remained in fully adjusted models, including Ruminococcus_B gnavus. Among others, inverse associations were observed for SFEL01 sp004557245 and Fimadaptatus sp900553645 from Christensenellales, an order in which butyrate production has been reported. Streptococcus mutans and Limosilactobacillus fermentum, oral-associated species previously associated with coronary atherosclerosis, were associated with a higher risk of incident IHD, which remained after adjustment for dental health. Replication analysis in the HUNT study supported the finding for S. mutans. No associations were observed with ischemic stroke. Conclusions: Gut species diversity and specific species abundance were associated with incident IHD, providing evidence supporting a protective role of two Christensenellales species and an adverse role of oral species and R. gnavus in the development of IHD.

papers.title: Projected prevalence and number of persons with diagnosed type 2 diabetes by socioeconomic position in Germany between 2022 and 2060
papers.abstract: BackgroundCurrent projections of the prevalence and number of persons with type 2 diabetes by socioeconomic position (SEP) are lacking for Germany. This study aims to project age-specific type 2 diabetes prevalence in Germany by sex and SEP between 2022 and 2060. MethodsWe used a partial differential equation (PDE) based on the illness-death model to project age-specific type 2 diabetes prevalence by sex and SEP between 2022 and 2060. The PDE describes the relationship between prevalence, incidence, all-cause mortality and the mortality rate ratio (MRR) of individuals with vs. without type2 diabetes considering age, calendar year and SEP. SEP was measured by quintiles of the German Index of Socioeconomic Deprivation (GISD). Baseline prevalence, incidence, and MRR in 2022 were derived from statutory health insurance data ([~]85% of the German population). Projected prevalence was multiplied by population projections from the German Federal Statistical Office to estimate the number of persons with diabetes. ResultsType 2 diabetes prevalence increases with age, peaking between 80 and 90 years. Between 2022 and 2060, age-specific prevalence is projected to increase for both sexes across all SEP groups. SEP-related disparities persisted with largest differences between the highest (5th GISD quintile) and lowest (1st GISD quintile) SEP group. The number of persons with type 2 diabetes is projected to rise from 8.4 million in 2022 to between 11.2 and 19.2 million in 2060. ConclusionsBetween 2022 and 2060, age-specific type 2 diabetes prevalence is projected to increase with increasing socioeconomic inequalities.

papers.title: Investigating Differential Changes in Cardiovascular Mortality by Documented diabetes in the United States Before and During the COVID-19 Pandemic: A Comparative Time-Series Analysis
papers.abstract: BackgroundWhether diabetes modified pandemic-related changes in cardiovascular disease (CVD) mortality remains uncertain. We examined differential changes in US CVD mortality among deaths with versus without diabetes documented on the death certificate. MethodsWe analyzed CDC WONDER Multiple Cause of Death data from 2005 to 2024, identifying deaths with CVD as the underlying cause among adults aged [≥]25 years. Cohorts were CVD deaths with diabetes documented as a contributing cause (CVD+DM) and CVD deaths without documented diabetes. Because pre-2020 trajectories differed, the primary comparison of age-adjusted rates used a comparative interrupted time-series model allowing cohort-specific pre-2020 trends. Difference-in-differences estimates (2015-2019 vs 2020-2024) were descriptive. ResultsCVD+DM mortality declined from 43.1 per 100,000 in 2005 to 34.3 in 2019 and was 38.4 in 2024; mortality without documented diabetes declined from 398.7 to 296.6 and was 289.8. In the primary analysis, CVD+DM mortality showed a 13.1% greater relative level increase at 2020 (95% CI, 10.4%-15.9%), with no significant differential change in slope thereafter. Descriptively, the ratio of rate ratios was 1.16, and the absolute difference-in-differences was 5.0 per 100,000. ConclusionsAfter accounting for cohort-specific pre-2020 trends, CVD mortality with documented diabetes showed a greater relative increase at the 2020 transition. These findings describe differential mortality patterns rather than a causal effect of diabetes or the pandemic. WHAT IS NEW?O_LICardiovascular disease mortality with documented diabetes showed a 13% greater relative level increase at the 2020 transition than cardiovascular disease mortality without documented diabetes, after accounting for pre-2020 trends. C_LIO_LIThe difference was concentrated in the level change around 2020, with no significant differential change in slope thereafter. C_LIO_LIFindings were directionally consistent across analyses using alternative baseline periods, breakpoints, and restriction to type 2 diabetes. C_LI WHAT ARE THE CLINICAL IMPLICATIONS?O_LIThe findings suggest that people with coexisting cardiovascular disease and diabetes may warrant particular attention during periods of major health system disruption, including efforts to maintain continuity of cardiometabolic care. C_LIO_LIBecause the analysis is based on death-certificate documentation, the findings should be interpreted as a population-level mortality signal rather than evidence that diabetes caused the observed mortality difference. C_LI

papers.title: Sex specificity in DNA Methylation Profiles of Neonates Following Early Preterm Birth
papers.abstract: Preterm birth (PTB) affects 11% of pregnancies worldwide, yet the biological mechanisms underlying its etiology remain unclear. We conducted a sex-stratified epigenome-wide association study of newborn saliva DNA methylation in 273 mother-child pairs from the Peruvian Placental Abruption Genetic Epidemiology (PAGE) study. Robust linear regression models adjusted for maternal, cellular, and technical factors identified 318 and 542 ePTB-associated CpG sites and 784 and 1,401 differentially methylated regions in boys and girls, respectively, with limited overlap between sexes. Functional analyses revealed enrichment of signals in Open Sea regions and pathways related to neurodevelopment, neural function, fetal growth, cellular organization, transcription factors, and microRNAs. Several associations replicated findings from prior studies of PTB, gestational age, and post-menstrual age. These results identify sex-specific epigenetic signatures of ePTB in an Admixed-American population and highlight developmental and regulatory pathways associated with ePTB.

papers.title: A deterministic framework for linkage of infectious disease surveillance and national mortality records: development and validation using tuberculosis surveillance data
papers.abstract: BackgroundLinkage of infectious-disease surveillance data to mortality records is important for estimating long-term outcomes, but incomplete personal identifiers present methodological challenges. We developed and validated a deterministic linkage framework for linking the National Tuberculosis Surveillance System (NTBS) with Office for National Statistics (ONS) mortality records. MethodsTB notifications in England from 2001-2024 were linked to ONS mortality records using 12 sequential matching rules based on combinations of NHS number, date of birth, name, postcode, sex and phonetic matching. Linkage outputs underwent person-level deduplication and clerical review. Precision and recall were estimated, and potential linkage bias assessed by variation in identifier completeness and linkage success. Confirmed false-positive links identified during validation were removed from the analytical dataset. ResultsAmong 151,965 TB notifications, 28,060 initial links were identified. Following deduplication, validation and refinement, 26,937 linked notifications were retained. Estimated precision increased from 97.7% to 99.2% (95% CI 96.8-100.0) following removal of false-positive links; estimated recall was 98.1% (95% CI 95.4-98.6%). More than 90% of links used NHS-number-based match keys. PDS enrichment increased NHS-number availability and enabled additional NHS-number-based links, although a small proportion linked to different ONS records following enrichment. NHS number availability and linkage success differed across demographic and social groups, demonstrating differential linkage. ConclusionsA hierarchical deterministic approach combined with targeted validation achieved high linkage accuracy while identifying and addressing differential linkage. This provides a transparent framework for future NTBS-ONS linkage and may be adaptable to other surveillance systems where comparable identifiers are available. Key messagesO_LIHierarchical deterministic linkage achieved high precision (>99%) and recall (>96%) when linking tuberculosis notifications to mortality records. C_LIO_LIValidation demonstrated that high linkage accuracy can be achieved using routinely collected identifiers within national surveillance data. C_LIO_LIThe validated linkage provides a robust framework for mortality ascertainment and long-term outcome monitoring within tuberculosis surveillance. C_LI

papers.title: Real-world effectiveness of nirsevimab over three RSV seasons in an integrated health care system: a target trial emulation study
papers.abstract: Most nirsevimab effectiveness estimates come from test-negative designs, which restrict populations to those seeking healthcare and testing. We estimated nirsevimab effectiveness among infants six months post-receipt using a target trial emulation with an estimand aligned to phase 3 trials. We emulated a target trial among infants born from February 2, 2023 through May 30, 2026, using electronic medical records at Kaiser Permanente Georgia. Using a g-computation estimator with Cox models fit separately in nirsevimab recipients and non-recipients, we estimated the cumulative incidence of RSV hospitalization and medically-attended RSV at 30-day intervals through 180 days post-receipt. Among 4,826 infants, nirsevimab reduced the risk of RSV hospitalization by 95% (95% CI: 84% to 98%) and medically-attended RSV by 67% (95% CI: 45% to 80%) at 180 days post-receipt. The number needed to immunize to prevent one case was 147 (95% CI: 94 to 333) for RSV hospitalization and 39 (95% CI: 28 to 68) for medically-attended RSV. Nirsevimab was effective through 180 days post-receipt. This cohort-based emulation avoids conditioning on testing and the restricted generalizability of the test-negative and matching-based designs that dominate the literature. These findings support continued nirsevimab use to protect infants against RSV.

papers.title: Intersectional inequalities in demand satisfied by modern contraceptive methods among women in sub-Saharan Africa, 1994 to 2024: a multilevel analysis of individual heterogeneity and discriminatory accuracy
papers.abstract: BackgroundDemand for family planning satisfied by modern methods is Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) indicator 3.7.1, and countries have committed to universal access to family planning by 2030. Inequalities are usually reported one social dimension at a time. This hides how social characteristics combine and leaves open whether programmes should target social groups or strengthen services for all women. We measured intersectional inequalities in demand satisfied by modern methods among women in sub-Saharan Africa over three decades, assessed how well social position discriminates between women, and identified groups left behind. Methods and findingsWe did a preregistered cross-sectional analysis of 139 Demographic and Health Surveys from 38 countries with fieldwork from 1994 to 2024. We included 675,584 women aged 15-49 years with demand for family planning and grouped them into 144 intersectional strata by age, union status, education, household wealth and residence. We fitted multilevel logistic models with random effects for strata and surveys (multilevel analysis of individual heterogeneity and discriminatory accuracy, MAIHDA) and estimated the variance partition coefficient (VPC), the area under the curve (AUC) and the proportional change in variance (PCV). Weighted demand satisfied rose from 27.5% in 1994-99 to 54.1% in 2018-24. Predicted demand satisfied ranged from 13.2% (95% CI: 11.0 -15.9) among married adolescents with no schooling in the poorest rural households to 68.0% (95% CI: 63.6 - 72.0) among unmarried urban women aged 25-34 years with secondary schooling in the richest households. The strata explained only 6.9% (95% CI: 5.6 - 8.7) of individual variation, with small discriminatory accuracy (AUC = 0.65; 95% CI: 0.63 - 0.66), and a Bayesian model gave a similar VPC (7.0%; 95% credible interval: 5.7 - 8.9). Additive effects explained 95.1% of the between-stratum variance. The VPC fell from 10.1% (95% CI: 8.0 - 12.8) in 1994-99 to 4.5% (95% CI: 3.6 - 5.8) in 2018-24. Five strata of married rural women with no schooling were in the lowest decile in every period. In the latest surveys, married rural women aged 15-24 years with no schooling had lower demand satisfied than other women in 29 of 30 countries (median gap 17.5 percentage points). The 15 most disadvantaged strata held a median 16.4% of unsatisfied demand, so targeting these groups alone would reach about one in six women whose demand is not met. The main limitations are the cross-sectional design, self-reported contraceptive use and the exclusion of 15 early surveys. ConclusionsIntersectional gaps in demand satisfied by modern methods have narrowed in sub-Saharan Africa, and most of the remaining gap between groups is additive. Social position alone discriminates poorly between women, so programmes targeted only by social group would miss most women with unmet need. This supports strengthening universal services. Within universal services, married adolescents and young women with no schooling in poor rural households have been left behind for three decades in almost every country and need priority, country-specific programmes if the 2030 targets are to be met. Author summaryO_ST_ABSWhy was this study done?C_ST_ABSO_LISustainable Development Goal 3.7 commits countries to universal access to family planning by 2030, and the share of women whose demand is satisfied by modern methods is the main indicator of progress. C_LIO_LIGaps in this indicator are usually reported by one characteristic at a time, such as age or wealth, although women live at the intersection of several characteristics. C_LIO_LIProgramme managers need to know whether to target particular social groups or to strengthen services for all women, and which groups, if any, have been left behind. C_LI What did the researchers do and find?O_LIWe analysed 675,584 women with demand for family planning in 139 national surveys from 38 sub-Saharan African countries between 1994 and 2024, grouped into 144 combinations of age, marital status, schooling, wealth and residence. C_LIO_LIDemand satisfied ranged from 13% to 68% across groups, but group membership explained only 7% of the differences between individual women, and the gaps between groups halved over three decades. C_LIO_LIMarried adolescents and young women with no schooling in poor rural households were among the most disadvantaged groups in every period, and in the latest surveys they lagged behind other women in 29 of 30 countries by a median of 17.5 percentage points. C_LI What do these findings mean?O_LITargeting family planning programmes only by social characteristics would miss most women whose demand is not met, so universal services should remain the foundation. C_LIO_LIMinistries of health and FP2030 partners should give priority to married adolescents and young women with no schooling in rural areas, and should report SDG indicator 3.7.1 for this group alongside the national average. C_LIO_LIThe study describes associations from self-reported cross-sectional survey data and cannot identify the causes of these gaps. C_LI

papers.title: Direction of apoB/LDL-C Discordance and Systemic Inflammation in U.S. Adults
papers.abstract: BackgroundApolipoprotein B (apoB) and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) are established biomarkers of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) that tend to be closely correlated. However, some individuals have discordant apoB and LDL-C. We evaluated whether apoB/LDL-C discordance is associated with elevated high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP), a key marker of systemic inflammation, in a nationally representative sample. Methods and ResultsWe analyzed cross-sectional data of 2226 adults aged 20 years or older from the 2015 to 2016 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey with complete apoB, LDL-C, and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP). LDL-C and apoB were converted to survey-weighted z scores, and discordance was the residual of apoB regressed on LDL-C. Participants were classified as apoB-high, LDL-C-high, or concordant (reference). The association of discordance group with elevated hs-CRP (>3 mg/L) was estimated with survey-weighted logistic regression, adjusted for age, sex, body mass index (BMI), and diabetes. Discordance was present in 26.4% of adults (13.7% apoB-higher, 12.6% LDL-C-higher). Elevated hs-CRP prevalence differed by discordance group: 47.6% (95% CI, 37.6-57.7) in the apoB-high group versus 20.5% (12.9-28.1) in the LDL-C-high group and 33.6% (29.7-37.4) in the concordant group. Relative to concordant participants, adjusted odds of elevated hs-CRP were higher for apoB-high discordance (odds ratio [OR], 1.58; 95% CI, 1.03-2.45) and lower for LDL-C-high discordance (OR, 0.49; 95% CI, 0.30-0.78). Similar results were obtained among participants not on statin therapy, with apoB-high discordance demonstrating stronger adjusted odds of elevated hs-CRP (OR, 2.02; 95% CI, 1.01-4.04). ConclusionDiscordantly high apoB relative to LDL-C is associated with systemic inflammation in a nationally representative sample of U.S. adults.

papers.title: Smoking trajectories and brain health in middle-aged adults: a 15-year longitudinal study
papers.abstract: BackgroundSmoking is a prevalent and preventable risk factor for poor brain health. These habits often establish in early adulthood and have lasting consequences, yet most research focuses on later-life smoking, overlooking important prevention windows. We examined smoking trajectories from early adulthood in relation to midlife brain health. MethodsIn 1,900 adults (65.6% female, mean age 32.5 years) from the Dutch population-based Generation R Study (ORACLE subset), smoking was assessed five times over 15 years, from before pregnancy to midlife. K-means clustering identified smoking trajectories, alongside measures of current smoking, pack-years, and abstinence years. At mean age 47.7 years, MRI assessed gray and white matter volumes, white-matter hyperintensity volume, cerebrovascular markers, and vertex-wise cortical thickness and surface area. FindingsFive trajectories were identified: non-smoking (63%), quitting before pregnancy (12%), quitting during/after pregnancy (11%), relapsing (9%), and persistent smoking (4%). All compared with non-smoking, quitting before pregnancy was associated with 6.57 cm3 larger gray matter (95%CI[0.27,12.87],p=.041), 7.71 cm3 larger white matter (95%CI[0.77,14.65],p=.030), and larger cortical surface area in bilateral middle/inferior temporal regions. Quitting during/after pregnancy was associated with more lacunes (OR=2.39; 95%CI[1.23,4.68],p=.011), but similar brain volumes. Relapsing was associated with 0.15 standard deviations more white matter hyperintensity volume (95%CI[0.00,0.30],p=.045) and thinner regions in the right cortex. Persistent smoking had double white matter hyperintensities (0.31 standard deviations; 95%CI[0.10,0.50], p=.003) and widespread bilateral thinner cortices. Similarly, single-timepoint measures like current smoking (vs never smoking) were linked to 9.72 cm3 smaller gray matter volume (95%CI[-16.53,-2.19],p=.005), 0.17 standard deviations more hyperintensity volume (95%CI[0.03,0.32],p=.015), and widespread thinner cortices. Each additional pack-year was associated with 0.45 cm3 smaller gray matter volume (95%CI[-0.85,-0.06],p=.025); each additional abstinence year was associated with 0.01 standard deviations less hyperintensity volume (95%CI[-0.02,0.00],p=.022). InterpretationSmoking trajectories from early adulthood and midlife are associated with midlife brain health, supporting early and sustained smoking cessation. FundingHorizonEurope Research and Innovation Programme (HappyMums, grant agreement No 101057390); European Research Council (TEMPO, grant agreement No 101039672; ORACLE, grant agreement No 678543).

papers.title: Age at Menopause and Dementia Risk: Blood-Based Biomarker Evidence from a US National Study
papers.abstract: ImportanceEarlier age at menopause associates with increased later life dementia risk, but the biological links that underlie this relationship remain poorly understood in population-based samples. ObjectiveTo evaluate the relationship between history of menopausal timing and AD/ADRD-related blood-based biomarkers in postmenopausal women. DesignObservational study using the U.S. Health and Retirement Study. AD/ADRD-related biomarkers were measured from venous blood draws conducted in 2016 and released in 2025. We estimated linear and nonlinear associations between spontaneous menopause timing and biomarkers, accounting for sociodemographic and health covariates. We evaluated effect modification by APOE 4 carrier status. Secondary analyses evaluated associations with hysterectomy history. SettingPopulation-based. ParticipantsCommunity-dwelling post-menopausal women aged 65 years or older. ExposurePrimary: Self-reported spontaneous age of menopause among women with no history of hysterectomy. Secondary: Self-reported history of hysterectomy (oophorectomy history was not assessed). Main Outcomes and MeasuresNeurofilament light chain (NfL) and glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) measured in plasma, and phosphorylated tau (p-tau181) and growth differentiation factor 15 (GDF-15), measured in serum, by Simoa or ELLA. ResultsAmong 1449 women [≥] 65 years, 38.4% self-reported a hysterectomy. Among 893 postmenopausal women without a history of hysterectomy (mean [SD] age at biomarker collection, 75.2 [7.2] years; mean age at menopause, 50.2 [5.2] years), menopausal timing was nonlinearly associated with NfL. Between menopausal ages 45-50, menopause timing was associated with higher NfL (0.010 SD units/year, [95% CI: -0.007, 0.027]), while from menopausal ages 50-55, the association reversed (b= -0.031, [95% CI: -0.051, -0.011]). Associations with GFAP or pTau-181 were not significant, but were directionally similar to those observed for NfL. Later menopausal timing linearly associated with lower GDF-15 (b = -0.015, [95% CI: -0.027, -0.004]). Self-reported hysterectomy was associated with higher GDF-15 (b= 0.118, [95% CI: 0.015, 0.220]), but not other biomarkers. Associations did not significantly differ by APOE {varepsilon}4 status. Conclusions and RelevanceIn a nationally representative study, earlier age at menopause in midlife was associated with later life AD/ADRDs biomarkers reflecting neuroaxonal degeneration and inflammation, underscoring the importance of understanding reproductive aging in dementia risk. KEY POINTSO_ST_ABSQuestionC_ST_ABSWhat is the association between menopausal timing and blood-based Alzheimers disease and related dementias (AD/ADRD) biomarkers among postmenopausal women 65 years and older in the United States? FindingsMenopausal timing is associated with higher NfL in women who experienced menopause before age 50, but lower NfL in women with menopausal ages after 50. Earlier menopausal timing is linearly associated with higher GDF-15. Secondary analyses showed associations between hysterectomy history and higher GDF-15. MeaningYounger menopausal timing associates with higher AD/ADRD-related biomarkers measured decades later in a population-based cohort, underscoring a link between reproductive aging and future neurodegenerative risk.

papers.title: Weighting the weeks that matter: entropic tilting for epidemic forecast evaluation
papers.abstract: The performance of infectious disease forecasting models is commonly calculated under the implicit assumption that forecast accuracy is equally important across time. This approach may obscure or under-weight differences in model performance during the epidemic periods that matter most for public-health decisions. Here, we introduce the weighted prequential score (WPS), a forecast evaluation framework that can emphasize epidemic periods of interest. The WPS is a weighted average of scores over time, where weights are constructed through entropic tilting which up-weights priority periods while keeping the WPS as close as possible to the arithmetic average. We demonstrate the WPS on forecasts of incident hospitalizations submitted to the CDC FluSight challenge, focusing on two priority periods: weeks of rapid growth in incidence and weeks near the seasonal peak. Across season-location-horizon pairs, doubling the weight assigned to priority periods changes the top-ranked model in 10%-26% of eligible settings, while the top-ranked model remains unchanged regardless of the amount of weight assigned in 37%-68% of settings. We demonstrate that for suitable weights, the models favored by the WPS yield an average gain in accuracy during priority periods that is at least as large as the average accuracy lost during the remaining weeks. Because weights can be defined using observed outcomes, the WPS is not a proper scoring rule. Hence, we recommend using the WPS as a retrospective evaluation diagnostic. The WPS can guide public-health practitioners in selecting models that perform well during periods most relevant to their decisions, while encouraging forecasting teams to improve accuracy during these critical weeks. Author summaryIn the context of public health decisions, the importance of accurate infectious disease forecasts may vary over the course of an epidemic. For example, accurate forecasts of incident hospitalizations around the seasonal peak may be particularly important for hospital staffing decisions. We introduce a forecast scoring rule that allows users to emphasize accuracy during the epidemic phases most relevant to their decisions. We demonstrate our approach on forecasts of influenza hospitalization incidence, focusing on periods of rapid growth and weeks surrounding the seasonal peak. We find our approach leads to model rankings that prioritize accuracy during these periods with minimal losses in performance across the entire epidemic.

papers.title: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and Risk of Colorectal Cancer: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
papers.abstract: Epidemiologic studies suggest that type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is associated with an increased risk of colorectal cancer (CRC). However, prior meta-analyses have relied heavily on studies published more than a decade ago and have often combined distinct epidemiologic effect measures. We conducted an updated systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies published from January 2012 through January 2026 evaluating the association between T2DM and incident CRC. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, CENTRAL, and Scopus were searched, and eligible studies reporting associations between T2DM and CRC were included. Effect estimates were synthesized separately using random-effects models to calculate pooled estimates with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Sex-specific and leave-one-out sensitivity analyses were also conducted. Fourteen studies were included, comprising nine cohort and five case-control studies; six reported odds ratios (ORs), seven reported hazard ratios (HRs), and one reported a standardized incidence ratio (SIR). T2DM was associated with higher odds of incident CRC (OR, 1.28; 95% CI, 1.13-1.46) and a higher hazard of incident CRC (HR, 1.27; 95% CI, 1.23-1.31). The study reporting an SIR also showed higher CRC incidence among individuals with T2DM (SIR, 1.40; 95% CI, 1.39-1.45). Sex-specific analyses generally showed positive associations in both females and males, and sensitivity analyses supported the robustness of the pooled findings. Overall, T2DM was associated with an increased risk of incident CRC, with a consistent direction of association across distinct epidemiologic effect measures. These findings provide updated evidence supporting consideration of T2DM as a marker of increased CRC risk and may inform CRC prevention strategies among individuals with T2DM.

papers.title: Prevalence of Self-Reported Auditory Dysfunction Among Call Center Employees and Its Association with Shift Work Across Various Call Centers in Cairo, Egypt, March 2026
papers.abstract: BackgroundThe rapid, unregulated expansion of the call center industry in developing countries has increased occupational health risks for young adults, particularly with regard to auditory health. Prolonged exposure to acoustic trauma, long working hours, and the high intensity nature of call center work can negatively affect young adults at the start of their working lives and may contribute to permanent noise induced hearing loss (NIHL). This damage is often irreversible but preventable if identified at an early stage. This study aims to evaluate the burden of auditory impairment among call center employees in Egypt and to propose evidence based mitigation strategies. MethodsA pilot cross sectional study was conducted among employees of various medical call centers over approximately three months (January to March 2026). Participants were recruited through voluntary (self selected) sampling. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire on work history, and statistical analysis was performed to examine associations with work duration and intensity. Three semi structured, open ended interviews were conducted in March 2026 to explore the symptoms in greater depth. ResultsForty six call center employees completed the questionnaire. The most frequently reported symptoms were mishearing words (82.6%), difficulty understanding speech in background noise (80.4%), needing others to repeat themselves (78.3%), and sensitivity to loud sounds (78.3%); 60.9% reported tinnitus. Higher auditory symptom severity was associated with a history of acoustic shock (Mann Whitney U = 344.0, p = .004) and with greater cognitive symptom burden (Spearmans {rho} = .416, p = .004), but not significantly with shift type (p = .177), years of work (p = .885), or daily and weekly working hours. Qualitative interviews described auditory strain that builds through the shift, disrupted sleep, informal coping, and the absence of employer guidance or symptom reporting pathways. Conclusion and RecommendationsSelf reported auditory symptoms were common in this preliminary sample of call center employees and were associated with acoustic shock exposure and cognitive symptom burden, but not significantly with shift pattern or length of service. Because the study was cross sectional, relied on self reports, and used a small volunteer sample (pilot study), the findings cannot establish causation or true prevalence. Recommended measures include acoustic shock limiters with incident reporting, audiometric screening that prioritizes at risk employees, safe volume education with regular breaks, and educational programs on auditory hazards and early warning signs to prevent actual auditory damage. Larger multi site studies with audiometric confirmation are also needed.
